Figure 45. Simplified supply chain diagram for CdTe FTO coated front glass 3.5.1 Technology Trends for CdTe PV Glass CdTe PV modules use front and rear glass, which do not have identical specifications. Front glass: For First Solar products, the front glass acts as a superstrate, which requires a high degree of flatness as well as a TCO coating on the superstrate side. To achieve the necessary flatness, CdTe PV front glass is typically produced on a float line (Basore and Feldman 2022a). The front glass is annealed and has requirements for flatness to accommodate the thin-film layers, in addition to low iron content (for transparency). Heat strengthening of the glass occurs after the high-temperature CdTe deposition step (Meagley et al. 2025). Prior to CdTe absorber layer manufacturing, a thin-film TCO layer composed of FTO, indium tin oxide, and zirconium oxide is deposited on the smooth side of the float glass (Wikoff et al. 2022; Preeti and Kumar 2025). The front glass also has an antireflective coating (opposite side from the TCO), made of one or more metal oxides such as tin oxide (Guardian Glass 2021; Buskens et al. 2016; Thomsen et al. 2009). Rear glass. The rear glass serves primarily as a cover and does not require the same performance and characteristics as the front glass superstrate. While there are bifacial CdTe modules, they do not necessarily use an antireflective coating on the rear glass owing to additional cost (Ovaitt et al. 2024). Glass Thickness. Glass thicknesses vary for CdTe modules between front and back and across series (Table 8). Glass is typically annealed before delivery to the module production facility, where it undergoes heat strengthening during the CdTe deposition processes, per discussion with industry. Typically, heat strengthening creates safety glass (Palmiotti et al. 2025).
